items.title: Windows 10 Computer Use: blank Notepad capture times out at independently verified Medium and High integrity

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

Computer Use can discover, launch and activate Windows applications and read their UI Automation text, but cannot obtain window screenshots. A blank Windows Notepad reproduces:

```text
FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel
```

The same failure occurred in two independently measured startup contexts: Medium/non-elevated and High/elevated. Elevating the app did not provide a working capture workaround.

Potentially related: #52754 and #54469. This report adds a measured elevation comparison on different graphics hardware; a shared root cause is not established.

## Recorded test environment (17 October 2026)

- Windows 10, build 19045.
- ChatGPT Windows package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0.
- Bundled Computer Use skill/plugin build observed locally: 26.1013.40934 (not a separately verified native helper executable version).
- Workspace dependency bundle: 26.1015.12040.
- Reported native Codex version: 0.163.0-alpha.10.2.
- Intel HD Graphics 515; driver 27.20.100.9416.
- Built-in app update check reported `up_to_date`; dependency diagnostics reported healthy.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Keep Windows unlocked, with the target visible on the active desktop.
2. Initialize the bundled `@oai/sky` client through the supported Computer Use runtime.
3. Launch a blank Windows Notepad via `sky.launch_app`.
4. Use `sky.list_windows` to obtain its actual returned window; bind it via `sky.get_window` and activate it via `sky.activate_window`.
5. Call `sky.get_window_state({window, include_screenshot:true, include_text:true})`.
6. After the screenshot error, refresh window selection and call the same API with `include_screenshot:false, include_text:true`.

Expected: a screenshot of the selected blank Notepad.
Actual: screenshot times out; text-only returns the editor, menus and status bar (Ln 1, Col 1; 100%; Windows CRLF; UTF-8).

## Measured Medium/High comparison

| Test on 17 October (UTC) | Independently read process tokens | Screenshot | Text-only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medium instance: capture error recorded 21:03:18.076Z | ChatGPT, app-server, temporary command shell and both active capture helpers: TokenIsElevated=False; Medium S-1-16-8192; Limited | FrameArrived timeout | Success, 21:04:56.535Z |
| Fresh High instance: capture 21:22:41.530Z–21:22:43.950Z | Before capture at 21:22:21Z: ChatGPT, app-server and temporary command shell: TokenIsElevated=True; High S-1-16-12288; Full | Same FrameArrived timeout | Success, 21:22:58.077Z |

The High instance was started by the user using normal Windows UAC through the registered package launch route, with `--do-not-de-elevate`. The launcher recorded no existing ChatGPT processes before launch. A post-test token query at 21:23:02Z confirmed the same app instance remained High and both capture helpers were High/Full as well. Helper tokens were not sampled at the exact instant of the capture call.

There was one screenshot request per instance in this paired comparison, followed by text-only checks. Other earlier troubleshooting tests are separate.

## Checks already performed

- App/helper reconnection and full app restarts did not resolve capture.
- Windows Apps > ChatGPT > Repair completed; capture still failed afterward.
- A prior Windows Graphics Capture `IsSupported` query returned True; this is capability detection, not proof of working frame delivery.
- A separate sandbox-readiness marker read-permission issue was corrected, its banner disappeared, and one native read-only sandbox command succeeded. The screenshot failure remained.
- No app reset/reinstall, graphics-driver replacement, security disabling or custom capture workaround was performed for this comparison.
- Similar capture errors were recorded locally from 27 September; an exact regression version or proven last-working baseline is not established.

## Request

Please provide a supported fix or a narrowly scoped native capture diagnostic that can distinguish helper/frame delivery failure from Windows graphics compatibility and policy effects. The observed timeout alone does not identify the underlying cause.

This submission contains only a sanitized technical summary. No raw logs, screenshots, personal paths, account identifiers, credentials or conversation transcript are attached. No new capture or reproduction was run to prepare this submission.

items.title: Windows desktop: existing cloud project lacks a discoverable local-folder linking flow; legacy identity reconciliation needed

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Environment

Windows desktop package 26.1013.4894.0; app updater reports desktop 26.1013.40934, build 20770, production channel and up_to_date on 2026-10-18. Observation on an existing profile, not a clean-install reproduction.

## Observed problem

Existing cloud project cannot be reconciled through the inspected UI

An existing cloud project is visible in ChatGPT mode but absent from Codex mode. Its legacy local representation has exactly one root beneath .chatgpt-projects. The actual source repository exists elsewhere. The observed difference follows the installed selector's exclusion of mirror-only roots in Codex mode; this alone does not establish that all project lists should be identical across modes.

In this version, the inspected existing cloud-project settings and menus provide name, instructions, memory/library access, pin/section and deletion controls, but no existing-project folder-binding or identity-reconciliation flow. The new-project dialog offers folders but does not expose selection of this existing cloud project. No new project was submitted and no code uploaded during inspection.

Installed selector inspection indicates that simply appending a real source root to the legacy representation could make the native entry eligible while the cloud entry remains eligible in ChatGPT mode. The shared-identity map requires a unique, account-matching native/cloud backing association; changing roots alone does not establish that association. This is a code-path inference, not a live production mutation or full end-to-end duplicate reproduction.

Please provide a supported, account-validated conversion/link operation for an existing cloud project and its local source, preserving existing cloud and local chats, and ensure deletion semantics cannot act on an unexpected second visible representation. The user's original report that deleting one of two displayed entries removes both was not deliberately re-tested because that would risk their data.

## Recovery context and limits

This profile previously lost grouping state; related report #52713. An initial assistant-driven recovery also incorrectly retained four legacy identities alongside their mapped native cache aliases, producing four additional imports. Those recovery-induced duplicates were reconciled and survived a real restart with 18 backend projects and 18 resolved cache identities. They must not be attributed to spontaneous duplicate creation on an untouched profile. The cross-mode visibility/binding issue above remains unresolved.

No intentional deletion test, private identity injection, new cloud project, or code upload was performed to reproduce this issue. Please clarify whether a supported existing-project association flow is available for this version/account and investigate identity reconciliation if the observed state is unexpected.

Private project/chat names, personal paths, account and thread IDs, raw logs/settings/databases and screenshots are omitted. Drafted and submitted by Codex on behalf of the user with explicit authorization.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

## Environment

- App: ChatGPT desktop app with Codex
- App version: 26.1013.40934
- OS: macOS Sequoia 15.7.3
- Device: MacBook Air M4, 16 GB RAM
- Browser: Google Chrome
- Browser access mode: Full CDP access

## Problem

Codex can discover Chrome tabs and read page titles and URLs, but reading page content is extremely slow.

A simple test on https://example.com/ successfully returned the page body, but took 30,061 milliseconds. The body-reading call had a timeout of 30,000 milliseconds.

This makes browser-based research and automation impractical, especially when working with multiple pages, videos, and comments.

## Troubleshooting already performed

- Enabled Full CDP access.
- Restarted Chrome.
- Reset the browser-control session.
- Retested a normal webpage.

The problem persists.

## Expected behavior

Codex should be able to read ordinary webpage content and interact with browser tabs promptly, without taking approximately 30 seconds for a simple page-reading operation.

## Actual behavior

Tab discovery works, and page content can eventually be returned, but the operation takes approximately 30 seconds.

Available logs do not provide enough information to identify whether the delay occurs during browser bridging, debugger attachment, CDP communication, or page extraction.

## Feedback ID

01a149ec-7bd4-7821-8371-ab31032d9884

Please investigate the browser-control performance issue and advise whether there is a known workaround.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the ChatGPT desktop app with Codex on macOS.
2. Connect Codex to Google Chrome using the browser extension, with Full CDP access enabled.
3. Open a normal webpage, such as https://example.com/.
4. Ask Codex to read the page body or extract its text.
5. Observe the execution time.

Expected result:
Codex should read the page content within a few seconds.

Actual result:
The page body was successfully returned, but the operation took 30,061 milliseconds, almost exactly the 30,000 ms timeout configured for the call.

Additional observations:
- Chrome tab discovery works.
- Page titles and URLs can be retrieved.
- Reading page content is extremely slow.
- The same issue occurred after restarting Chrome and resetting the browser-control session.
- Full CDP access is already enabled.

Environment:
- ChatGPT desktop app with Codex, version 26.1013.40934
- macOS Sequoia 15.7.3
- MacBook Air M4, 16 GB RAM
- Google Chrome

I do not have a minimal code snippet because this operation was performed through Codex's built-in browser-control functionality rather than a standalone script. The available logs do not identify which stage causes the delay.

items.title: [Windows desktop] GPT-6.1 Sol sometimes auto-compacts at ~200k usage despite a displayed 475k context window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows 11, 64-bit laptop; Chinese UI; Codex desktop experience in the ChatGPT desktop application. The reporter describes the installed application as the latest available to them on 2026-10-18; the exact About-dialog app/build number and subscription tier have not been recorded. Read-only platform output from this reporting environment: `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64`.

The locally inspected model cache reports `client_version: "0.163.0"`; this is not an independently verified desktop app build number.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 x64 laptop.

### What issue are you seeing?

When using **GPT-6.1 Sol**, the reporter sometimes observes automatic context compaction after only **200-something-k tokens** have been used, although the context indicator advertises an effective window of **475k**.

“200-something-k” is the reporter's approximate observation, **not a measured exact token count or a captured trigger threshold**. No event-level usage/compaction trace has been collected for this report. It is not known whether the indicator and the trigger are using the same accounting scope.

This is filed separately from the main-versus-side-chat indicator report because it concerns **actual automatic-compaction timing while the larger capacity is advertised**, not merely a change in the displayed denominator.

#### Read-only local metadata and configuration check

A read-only inspection of the local `models_cache.json` on 2026-10-18 returned the following selected metadata (cache `client_version: "0.163.0"`; this is **not** asserted to be the desktop app version):

| Cached model slug | context_window | effective_context_window_percent | Arithmetic effective window |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| gpt-6.1-sol | 500000 | 95 | 475000 |
| gpt-6-astra | 272000 | 95 | 258400 |
| gpt-6-sol | 272000 | 95 | 258400 |
| gpt-6-luna | 272000 | 95 | 258400 |
| gpt-reserve | 272000 | 95 | 258400 |
| gpt-5.6-sol | 272000 | 95 | 258400 |
| gpt-5.6-terra | 272000 | 95 | 258400 |
| gpt-5.6-luna | 272000 | 95 | 258400 |
| codex-auto-review | 272000 | 95 | 258400 |

These are the entries present in this cache snapshot, not a claim about every model/account. The effective values above are arithmetic projections (`context_window * 95 / 100`), not independent measurements of each thread's live limit. The snapshot's `fetched_at` was `2026-10-18T07:06:51.533818200Z`.

A narrow read-only check of the normal user `config.toml` found `model = "gpt-6.1-sol"` and no explicit assignments to `model_context_window`, `model_auto_compact_token_limit`, `model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope`, or `model_catalog_json`. No project `.codex/config.toml` existed at the checked workspace location. This check does not resolve every possible managed/profile/session/backend override. No configuration or cache was edited.

In the inspected GPT-6.1 Sol cache entry, there was **no explicit auto-compaction-threshold field**. Therefore this cache snapshot supports the 475000 arithmetic window but **does not establish the runtime's actual automatic-compaction threshold**.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow; occurrence is intermittent and a deterministic reproducer is not yet available:

1. Continue a long conversation with GPT-6.1 Sol in the Windows desktop app.
2. Observe the context indicator advertising approximately **475k** capacity.
3. In some occurrences, automatic compaction begins when the reporter has observed only **200-something-k** usage.
4. Compare the displayed usage/capacity with the point at which automatic compaction is triggered.

The relationship to side-chat creation, model switching, resuming a thread, previous compactions, reasoning effort, and tool-output size has not been isolated. The current cached model metadata was inspected without editing it or forcing a new compaction.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please verify that the runtime is using the correct GPT-6.1 Sol metadata and that the compaction trigger and UI usage are reconciled.

This request does **not** assume that automatic compaction must wait until exactly 475000 tokens. A usable context window and a compaction threshold are separate concepts; appropriate headroom for output/reasoning or another documented accounting scope can justify an earlier trigger.

However, compaction at only a little over 200k with 475k advertised should have an understandable and correct explanation. Please check:
- Whether the resolved model window or compaction default has fallen back to a smaller model/catalog value.
- Whether the UI and trigger count different inputs, local estimates, reasoning, or reserved headroom.
- Whether any token accounting is stale or counted twice.
- Whether the indicator should expose the **actual compaction counter, threshold, and scope** so that users can distinguish intentional headroom from a defect.

If the runtime is using an incorrect limit or counter, correct it; if this timing is intentional, clarify it in the UI/documentation rather than suggesting all 475k are available before compaction.

### Additional information

Official configuration reference: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference documents separate `model_context_window`, `model_auto_compact_token_limit`, and `model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope` settings. It does not by itself explain the observed incident.

Related reports:
- #55007: this reporter's Windows main/side-chat context-indicator mismatch. A shared cause has not been established.
- #53336: GPT-6.1 Sol context and compaction-limit regression between turns on macOS.
- #53913: a different reporter documents reasoning-accounting overlap and compaction at about 255k/475k. That investigation's measurements and root-cause claim are **not** asserted as reproduced on this Windows environment.
- #54517: a now-closed report of compaction at 312k/475k with a different level of evidence; its existence/closure does not establish the outcome for this report.

Please link or consolidate reports if maintainers confirm the same underlying defect. No app fix, configuration workaround, exact trigger value, or loss of conversation content is claimed here. No raw conversation history, account identifiers, credentials, or project files are included.

The snapshot's `fetched_at` was `2026-10-18T07:06:51.533818200Z`.

The 500000/95 metadata is consistent with the main chat's displayed 475k. The other cached entries provide a concrete smaller-window baseline: **272000 raw / 258400 at 95%**, rather than an assumed 275000. Whether the side chat is incorrectly using that baseline, displaying stale metadata, selecting another runtime model, or intentionally using a separate limit is not established.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow, not yet a controlled minimal reproduction:

1. Use GPT-6.1 Sol in the Windows Codex desktop experience.
2. Inspect the main chat's context indicator; it shows approximately **475k** total capacity.
3. Open a side conversation from that chat.
4. Inspect the side chat's context indicator; the reporter sees a **200-something-k** capacity instead.
5. Compare both surfaces' selected model and reported capacity.

### What is the expected behavior?

If the side chat is using the same GPT-6.1 Sol model and eligible runtime configuration, its context indicator should resolve that model's correct effective context limit rather than silently reverting to a generic/older smaller-window value.

If side chats intentionally use a different model or a smaller context allocation, the UI should clearly identify that model/allocation and explain the difference. A misleading model label or capacity indicator should be corrected.

Please investigate whether this is display-only, model/catalog fallback, fork/side-chat initialization, or a real per-thread limit change; the report does not assume which.

### Additional information

Related: #53336 reports GPT-6.1 Sol changing from **475000 to 258400** between turns on macOS, with separate runtime/cache evidence. This submission adds a **Windows main-chat versus side-chat observation** and a current local cache snapshot. A shared cause is possible but unverified; please consolidate if appropriate.

items.title: [Desktop feature request] Add a per-tool Stop button inside expanded long-running tool cards

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Windows 11, 64-bit laptop; Chinese UI; Codex desktop experience in the ChatGPT desktop application. The reporter describes the installed application as the latest available to them on 2026-10-18; the exact About-dialog app/build number and subscription tier have not been recorded. Read-only platform output from this reporting environment: `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64`.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please let the user **expand a long-running tool card and manually click a Stop/Cancel button for that specific tool invocation**.

A long shell command, a polling/waiting operation, or another slow tool can run longer than the user wants. The tool card is the natural place to inspect that operation and stop it. Sending another chat message can leave the user waiting for a tool-call boundary; stopping an entire chat/turn is not the same interaction as cancelling one selected tool.

Proposed interaction:

1. Codex starts a tool operation and displays its tool card.
2. The user expands that card to inspect the running operation/output.
3. An explicit **Stop tool** action is available while that invocation is active.
4. Clicking it sends a cancellation request for that invocation. The card distinguishes **stopping**, **cancelled by user**, **completed**, and **cancellation failed/not supported** rather than optimistically claiming cancellation succeeded.
5. Output already produced remains visible, with the final status and exit information when available. The conversation can continue with the cancellation result.

Suggested acceptance criteria:
- The action is scoped to the selected invocation, including an identifiable nested invocation where supported; unrelated tool calls, chats, and application processes are not indiscriminately terminated.
- For local terminal commands, forward interruption/cancellation through the supported terminal/process lifecycle, and report whether the command actually exited.
- Where a tool supports cooperative cancellation only, expose that limitation honestly instead of promising immediate remote termination or rollback of completed side effects.
- Disable or remove the action after the invocation reaches a terminal state; handle completion racing with the user's click.
- Keep this action distinct from stopping the entire agent turn. Make any broader stop scope explicit before applying it.

### Additional information

This is a **feature request**, not a claim that a particular current cancellation mechanism is broken.

Related but distinct:
- #55001 reports a compact tool row still saying “Running” when its expanded command says “Ran”. Reliable status reconciliation is important for deciding when a Stop action is applicable.
- #53838 reports a Windows conversation stuck on Working without an available conversation Stop control. The request here is specifically an **expanded-card, per-tool** control.

Please consider this for the Windows desktop app and consistent desktop behavior where applicable.

items.title: Remote (Android) open times out on large threads while the host replies instantly

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
**Environment**

- Codex desktop `26.1013.4894.0` (MSIX) on Windows 11 `10.0.26300`
- Remote client: Android app (`app_server.client_name="codex_chatgpt_android_remote"`)

**Symptom**

Opening a long-running thread from the phone shows a load timeout and never renders. Short threads open normally, and the same threads load fine on the desktop client. Reported to feel worse after updating to `26.1013.4894.0`, but I have no measurements from earlier builds, so I am not claiming a regression.

**Measurements** (same machine, same Wi-Fi, 7 threads, opened one by one from the Android client)

| Thread (first 8 of id) | Items | `thread_items` size | Turns | Remote open |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a13b71` | 981 | 137.8 MB | 47 | **timeout** |
| `01a0f4c0` | 3,754 | 157.4 MB | 181 | **timeout** |
| `01a0f10a` | 3,786 | **5.9 MB** | 191 | **timeout** |
| `01a0f93c` | 81 | 0.1 MB | 4 | ok |
| `01a0f978` | 242 | 0.8 MB | 11 | ok |
| `01a0adb8` | 106 | 0.2 MB | 11 | ok |
| `01a0a36a` | 138 | 0.3 MB | 35 | ok |

Every failure has **≥981 items**; every success has **≤242 items**.

Size is not the explanation: `01a0f10a` is only **5.9 MB** and still times out. It carries 3,786 items but almost no image data. So this is not bandwidth, not image payload, and not the network.

**Host-side evidence** (sanitized desktop logs, same second as each failed open)

- The host answers immediately and without error: `thread_lifecycle: composing running thread resume response thread_id=01a13b71-…` lands in the same second as the request, with `errorCode=null`.
- No error code ever reaches the client — nothing like `-32003`. The request simply never completes on the remote side.
- The only client-side line is `Conversation state not found conversationId=…`, which also appears for threads that open fine; it is noise, not the cause.
- For the same threads, desktop-side `thread/read`, `thread/turns` and `thread/items/*` return in ~200 ms.

In short: the host prepares the whole history and replies at once; the remote client cannot get it across its timeout.

**How to reproduce**

1. Create a thread with ~1,000+ items (a long asset/image session reaches this in a few hundred turns).
2. Connect the Android remote client to the desktop host.
3. Open that thread remotely → timeout. Open a small thread → fine.
4. Open the same thread on the desktop → fine.

**Expected**

Remote open should behave like desktop: first screen renders quickly, older history streams in lazily. A thread should not have to transfer its entire item history before it becomes usable.

**Suggestion**

- Paginate hydration for remote clients: return the last N turns/items plus a cursor, and pull earlier ranges on scroll (`thread/items` already accepts ranges).
- Cap what a single `thread/resume` response may contain, independently of thread size.
- Secondary, size only: `imageGeneration.result` keeps the full PNG as base64 inside `item_json`. On this machine that is ~2 GB across 751 items, up to 971 MB in one thread. Keeping only `savedPath` would shrink payloads by 10–50× — worth doing, but it will not fix `01a0f10a`, which is 5.9 MB.

All numbers above are row counts and byte sizes from the local thread database. No conversation content, file paths, account identifiers, or credentials are included.

The reporter is using the latest desktop release available to them as of **2026-10-18**, in the Codex experience now accessed through the ChatGPT desktop application. The exact About-dialog build number has not been captured; “latest” is the reporter's description, not an independently verified release comparison.

Not provided.

- Windows 11, 64-bit laptop.

  `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64`
- The affected UI is displayed in Chinese.

### What issue are you seeing?

The terminal tool card presents contradictory execution states: its **collapsed/summary row still says that a command is running**, while the **expanded command entry says that it has run/completed**.

The reporter confirms that the command had already finished. The supplied screenshot shows these two labels at the same time, with the same visible PowerShell command prefix:

```text
Summary row:
正在运行 $r='C:\path\to\project';$b=Join-Path $r 'artifacts\verification\...'
[“Running …”]

Expanded command entry:
已运行 $r='C:\path\to\project';$b=Join-Path $r 'artifacts\verification\...'
[“Ran …”]
```

The surrounding turn also displays **“已处理 22秒”** (“Worked/processed for 22 seconds”). This is transcribed UI text, not an independently measured command runtime.

The screenshot is the basis for this report. Local account and project paths have been replaced with placeholders in the transcription. No exit code, tool-call ID, or process inspection is claimed from the screenshot.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow:

1. Use the Codex experience in the Windows desktop application.
2. In an existing conversation, let Codex run a PowerShell terminal command. In the reported instance, the user had asked for the current progress.
3. After the command has finished, inspect/expand its tool card.
4. Observe that the command entry displays **“已运行”** (“Ran”), while its summary/compact row still displays **“正在运行”** (“Running”).
5. Compare the two states in the same conversation view.

This is an observed UI inconsistency, not yet a deterministic minimal reproducer. The report does not establish whether a specific command, an interruption, a long conversation, or another timing condition is necessary. Reproduction frequency and persistence after reopening/restarting the app have not been measured.

### What is the expected behavior?

Once a terminal command has reached a terminal execution state, the summary and expanded presentation of **that same command** should agree.

- A completed command should not continue to be labelled “Running” in the compact row.
- If an outer tool group is still awaiting another operation after its nested terminal command has finished, the UI should distinguish the group's remaining activity from the completed command, rather than displaying the same command as still running.
- Completion/state reconciliation should update both presentations without requiring the user to navigate away or guess which state is authoritative.

### Additional information

**Impact:** The contradictory status makes it difficult to tell whether the user should keep waiting or continue. It can also encourage an unnecessary rerun of an already-completed command.

**Related:** #49131 describes an interrupted tool card staying on “Running” in the VS Code extension. This report concerns the Windows desktop application's compact-versus-expanded terminal status mismatch; the same interruption precondition has not been established here. Please link or merge if maintainers confirm a common underlying defect.

No internal root cause has been established. This report does not assert that the subprocess is hung, that a command failed, or that the model stopped responding; the reported defect is the inconsistent UI execution-state presentation.

items.title: 0.163.0: omitted provider auth.cwd panics on account/read after server cwd deletion, even for an unused provider

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Verified scope

Independently reproduced on macOS arm64 with a freshly launched `codex app-server` reporting 0.163.0. Each case uses an isolated temporary `CODEX_HOME`, no copied user configuration or authentication, and no inference request. The provider below is only a synthetic configuration entry; it is not selected. The default OpenAI provider remains selected.

The original user-visible symptom was a shared-daemon CLI session stuck at `Waiting for startup`. The controlled test below reproduces the unanswered `account/read` request and exact panic directly over stdio, without relying on the original daemon's unverified version or reproducing the TUI itself.

## Minimal configuration

```toml
[analytics]
enabled = false

[model_providers.repro]
name = "Repro"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1"
requires_openai_auth = false

[model_providers.repro.auth]
command = "/usr/bin/false"
```

There is deliberately no `model_provider = "repro"` and no `auth.cwd`. The loopback URL and command are synthetic placeholders. No actual provider credentials or endpoint are needed.

## Reproduction

1. Create a temporary `CODEX_HOME` containing only the configuration above, plus a separate empty startup directory.
2. From that startup directory, launch `codex app-server --listen stdio://`, keeping stdin open.
3. Send the following newline-delimited messages:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"clientInfo":{"name":"cwd-repro","version":"1"},"capabilities":{"experimentalApi":true}}}
{"method":"initialized"}
{"id":2,"method":"account/read","params":{"refreshToken":false}}
```

4. Wait for the response to request 2. It succeeds with `account: null` and `requiresOpenaiAuth: true`.
5. From a different directory/process, remove only the empty startup directory. Leave `CODEX_HOME` and the server running.
6. Send the same account request with a new ID:

```json
{"id":3,"method":"account/read","params":{"refreshToken":false}}
```

Request 3 receives no response within the five-second test deadline. The server process remains alive, and stderr records:

```text
protocol/src/config_types.rs:629:21:
provider auth cwd must resolve: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

All test servers were terminated after the experiment. The normal shared daemon and user configuration were not changed.

## Controls on fresh 0.163.0 servers

| Configuration | account/read before deletion | account/read after deletion | Matching panic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No provider definition | Success | Success | No |
| Unused provider above; auth.cwd omitted | Success | No response within 5 seconds; server alive | Yes |
| Same unused provider; add cwd = "/" to its auth table | Success | Success | No |

These results were reproduced in a second run. They establish an omitted-auth.cwd failure path on 0.163.0 without requiring an active custom provider.

## Source evidence

- `account/read` calls `read_account`, which reloads configuration through `load_latest_config(None)`: [workspace_routing.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor/workspace_routing.rs#L174-L242).
- That reload now uses a non-project configuration and a stable Codex-home fallback: [config_manager.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/config_manager.rs#L191-L221).
- However, `ModelProviderAuthInfo.cwd` still defaults through `default_provider_auth_cwd()`, which falls back to the process current directory and panics if it cannot be obtained: [config_types.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/protocol/src/config_types.rs#L568-L635).

The control results and exact panic support this narrower failure during configuration deserialization. An unused provider definition is sufficient; provider selection and a model request are not required.

## Relationship to #54408

#54408 was closed after the general account/config-loading failure was reported fixed for 0.163.0. The no-provider control above succeeds on 0.163.0, consistent with that fix. The omitted provider-auth cwd case still fails on a freshly launched 0.163.0 server. This report supplies a concrete remaining configuration-dependent path rather than assuming the original daemon was up to date. Related older reports: #50619 and #51152.

## Expected behavior and workarounds

An omitted auth cwd should resolve against a valid configuration base or return a handled error; it should not panic and leave the account request unanswered.

The original affected installation recovered with `codex --no-daemon`, or by stopping the daemon and launching a new session from an existing directory. The isolated test also succeeds with an explicit stable `auth.cwd`; choosing a suitable directory depends on the actual auth command.

All example names and paths are synthetic. No real local paths, project names, hostnames, credentials, provider endpoints, or private configuration are included.

### What issue are you seeing?

After replacing an iPhone 17 Pro Max with an iPhone 18 Pro Max using Apple's Quick Start migration, the Codex view in the ChatGPT mobile app no longer lists the PCs previously accessible from the old iPhone.

The new iPhone shows the initial "Connect a computer" screen, with "Scan QR code" and "Enter code manually", rather than the existing connected PCs. Please investigate this as a device-migration and connection-restoration bug.

The workflow involves eight PCs: four directly accessible and four at remote locations. An alternative remote-access method is available for the remote PCs, but rebuilding each connection is a workaround; it does not fix the failure to preserve or restore connection setup when replacing the phone. The old iPhone is no longer available.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Sequence reported from the actual migration:

1. Use Codex Remote on an iPhone 17 Pro Max with previously configured PC connections.
2. Migrate to an iPhone 18 Pro Max using Apple Quick Start.
3. Open ChatGPT on the new iPhone and select Codex.
4. Observe that the previously connected PCs are absent and only the new-computer pairing flow is offered.
5. Inspect an existing desktop host's Settings > Connections > Control this PC.

This was observed during one real phone migration; a second migration has not been performed to reproduce it.

### What is the expected behavior?

After a phone migration, existing connection settings should be preserved or recoverable through a supported, authenticated migration flow. If a new device needs additional authorization, the app should explain that and provide a way to recover the existing host list and reauthorize access, rather than presenting an empty initial-setup screen.

Please provide a recovery path that does not require independently reopening the pairing setup on every PC whenever the phone is replaced. Necessary account and device verification should still apply.

### Additional information

Desktop evidence, transcribed from the inspected host's screenshot:

- "Allow connections" is ON.
- The authorized-device list still contains an iPhone entry labeled "iOS 27.0.1 iPhone", with its last connection shown as 14 hours earlier.
- The list also contains two Windows-client entries.
- The iPhone entry contains no iPhone 17/18 model name. Its identity as the old or new phone cannot be established from that label alone.

These observations establish that an iPhone authorization entry remains on at least one inspected host while the replacement phone cannot discover the previous PCs. They do not establish that any server-side record was deleted or identify the underlying authentication/storage cause.

Environment and diagnostic limits:

- Previous phone: iPhone 17 Pro Max.
- Replacement phone: iPhone 18 Pro Max.
- Migration method: Apple Quick Start.
- Exact ChatGPT mobile and desktop app versions, desktop host OS/build, and subscription: not recorded.
- The iOS version above is the label in the host's device list, not a separately verified OS version from the new phone.
- Matching account/workspace selection on the new phone and host has not yet been independently verified.
- Pairing storage, keychain state, and device identity have not been inspected.

Please investigate whether connection/authentication metadata fails to migrate, whether an existing recovery mechanism is not being offered, and how affected users can restore their connections. If device authorization intentionally cannot transfer, please document that limitation and provide a supported migration/recovery workflow.

items.title: ChatGPT Chrome extension 1.26.1005.11759: kernel fetch proxy throws "Response with null body status cannot have body" on 204/205/304

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

Codex Desktop with bundled Chrome plugin 26.1007.21434. The bug is in the ChatGPT Chrome extension itself, version 1.26.1005.11759 (extension ID `hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg`). That is the current Web Store version: an update check on 2026-10-18 returned 1.26.1005.11759.

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu), Google Chrome 155.0.8059.39 stable

### What issue are you seeing?

The extension's Errors page keeps showing this, with the source in `chunks/js-kernel-host-*.js`:

```
TypeError: Failed to construct 'Response': Response with null body status cannot have body
```

It comes back after clearing the errors and after updating. In our case it showed up next to the kernel's Statsig `https://ab.chatgpt.com/v1/initialize` request.

**Cause, read from the shipped code (1.26.1005.11759):**

The JS kernel's `fetch` is proxied through the background service worker.

1. `background.js`, the fetch handler (class with `fetches`/`abortFetch`), does the real `fetch` and returns:
   ```js
   { body: i.body == null ? null : base64(new Uint8Array(await i.arrayBuffer())), headers: [...i.headers], status: i.status, statusText: i.statusText }
   ```
2. `chunks/js-kernel-host-*.js`, the kernel-side `fetch(e, {signal, ...init})`, rebuilds the response:
   ```js
   s.status === 0 ? Response.error() : new Response(s.body == null ? null : fromBase64(s.body), s)
   ```

In Chrome 155 (tested in a page context), a fetched 204, 205 or 304 response has a **non-null** `body` (an empty stream). Step 1 therefore sends `body: ""`. Step 2 turns that into a zero-length `Uint8Array` and calls `new Response(Uint8Array(0), {status: 204, ...})`. The Fetch spec requires the constructor to throw for a null-body status, so **every kernel-proxied fetch that receives a 204, 205 or 304 rejects** instead of resolving.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This reproduces the browser behaviour without the extension: a standalone page in a fresh headless Chrome 155 profile, served by a local server that returns empty 204/205/304/200 responses.

```js
for (const st of [204, 205, 304, 200]) {
  const r = await fetch('/s/' + st, { cache: 'no-store' });
  // Chrome 155: r.body is non-null (0 bytes) for every status
  try { new Response(new Uint8Array(0), { status: r.status }); console.log(st, 'ok'); }
  catch (e) { console.log(st, String(e)); }
}
```

Output (GET and POST give the same result):

```
204 bodyNull=false bytes=0 -> TypeError: Failed to construct 'Response': Response with null body status cannot have body
205 bodyNull=false bytes=0 -> TypeError: ...
304 bodyNull=false bytes=0 -> TypeError: ...
200 bodyNull=false bytes=0 -> ok
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A 204, 205 or 304 seen by the kernel should resolve as a normal `Response` with a null body. A fix in either place works:

```js
// background.js: don't serialise a body for null-body statuses
const NULL_BODY = new Set([101, 103, 204, 205, 304]);
body: (i.body == null || NULL_BODY.has(i.status)) ? null : base64(...)

// and/or js-kernel-host: don't pass one
new Response((s.body == null || NULL_BODY.has(s.status)) ? null : fromBase64(s.body), s)
```

### Additional information

- Any kernel code path that receives one of these statuses is affected, not only Statsig. We have not traced which other endpoints the kernel reaches through this proxy.
- A separate, smaller issue in the same build: `mark_tab` wraps any `markTab` failure as "Please update the ChatGPT extension in Google Chrome to the latest version to continue." The background `markTab` can also fail on `requireSessionTab` (a tab no longer in the agent session) or on a status other than `handoff`/`deliverable`, but the message always tells the user to update. On the latest version that sends them in a loop; including `cause.message` in the user-facing error would fix it.

items.title: Codex quota drain: weekly usage 26%→67% during one turn and its subagents

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary

The original report described an apparent return of rapid quota drain around **October 16, 2026**, including the user's observation that a simple prompt used about **10 percentage points** of the allowance. A follow-up audit on October 19 adds measured local evidence and source analysis.

**The original isolated 10-point claim has not been reproduced.** The measurable case below is a long development turn with hundreds of model responses and subagents. It shows substantial processing and a correlated weekly allowance increase; it does not establish incorrect billing or prove an October 16 server regression.

### A concrete October 18 case

In one parent turn, from **08:12:59.067 to 11:49:21.080 UTC**:

| Measurement | Observed value |
|---|---:|
| Parent model / reasoning setting | GPT-6 Astra / high |
| Parent response records | 378 |
| Parent input tokens | 108,956,988 |
| Cached input, included in input | 107,904,640 (99.03%) |
| Parent output, including reasoning | 338,002 |
| Parent input + output | 109,294,990 |
| Child responses attributed to the same `root_turn_id` | 160 across 3 child sessions |
| Child input + output | 22,140,012 |
| Combined parent + children | **538 responses; 131,435,002 tokens** |

The parent's logged `codex` allowance snapshots changed from **26% used at 08:13:06.874 UTC** to **67% used at 11:48:55.291 UTC**: **41 percentage points**. Both endpoints report `window_minutes=10080`, `resets_at=1792875869`, and `plan_type=prolite`. One intermediate snapshot's reset timestamp differs by one second; the evidence preserves that difference. `secondary` is null.

These are account-level snapshots, not a per-turn invoice. Concurrent child work is included above, and other devices or unrecorded activity cannot be excluded. A short user message can trigger substantial continued work; this is not a fresh-chat, one-response test.

**Expected behavior:** users should be able to see and bound sustained work and allowance consumption within a turn. Recorded usage representations should make their treatment of compaction clear, and the provider should be able to reconcile allowance changes against the work actually performed.

## Environment and evidence window

- Inspected host: macOS **27.0.1**, build **26A434**, Apple silicon `arm64`.
- Installed desktop application: **ChatGPT 26.1013.40934**, build **20770**, containing the Codex desktop integration and bundled **`codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`**. Rollout originator metadata says `Codex Desktop`.
- Usage-bearing session creation metadata records **`0.162.0-alpha.17.2`** (53 sessions) and **`0.163.0-alpha.10.2`** (27). Creation metadata does not identify the binary used for every resumed request. The inspected app/OS versions are current observations, not independently established incident-time versions.
- Measurement window: **2026-10-14 00:00:00 UTC inclusive to 2026-10-19 00:00:00 UTC exclusive** (October 14 03:00 through October 19 03:00 Europe/Sofia).
- All 8,721 retained allowance snapshots have `limit_id=codex`, `plan_type=prolite`, a **10,080-minute primary window**, and no secondary window. This clarifies the recorded window without retroactively identifying which UI window the original 10% observation referred to.
- Current configuration has a custom `model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000` and no explicit `rollout_budget` section. Historical effective configuration was not reconstructed. This is not a stock-configuration benchmark.

## Five-day measured totals

The extractor read **86 indexed rollout files**, including records before the window to establish cumulative-counter baselines. **80 sessions** have usage in the window. No selected indexed files were missing.

| Per-response ledger metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Distinct response IDs | 8,003 |
| Input tokens | 1,891,196,885 |
| Cached input, included in input | 1,862,936,448 (**98.51%**) |
| Uncached input | 28,260,437 |
| Output tokens, including reasoning | 4,422,925 |
| Reasoning output, included in output | 1,959,007 |
| Input + output | **1,895,619,810** |

Cached input and reasoning output are not added twice. These are recorded token counts, not unique text, full-price tokens, or a monetary bill.

| UTC date | Response records | Input + output |
|---|---:|---:|
| October 14 | 457 | 67,654,551 |
| October 15 | 2,402 | 638,143,938 |
| October 16 | 3,002 | 694,844,243 |
| October 17 | 1,319 | 296,127,204 |
| October 18 | 823 | 198,849,874 |

High processing volume was already present on October 15. Daily totals are not a controlled before/after comparison: task mix, model, reasoning settings, context sizes and subagent activity vary. The dataset cannot establish a new metering multiplier or deployment date.

## Source analysis at pinned versions

Inspected tag `rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10.2`, whose annotated tag resolves to commit **`4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4`**. The preceding recorded tag resolves to **`740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74`**. The hashes here are commit IDs, not annotated-tag-object IDs.

1. **One user turn can contain many sampling requests.** The [turn loop rebuilds each request from retained history](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L454-L572), and [continues for model follow-up or pending input](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L578-L625). This supports the observed amplification mechanism. It does not show that every step was avoidable.
2. **Allowance percentages come from server-provided rate-limit data.** The [rate-limit parser maps the received percentages and windows](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/codex-api/src/rate_limits.rs#L135-L177); [session state publishes them alongside token information](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs#L5143-L5190). Local token sums alone cannot reconstruct the provider's subscription charging formula.
3. **Two local usage representations disagree around compaction.** [Ordinary sampling updates both response-level and cumulative usage](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L3092-L3110), with the [response ledger persisted separately](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs#L5010-L5033). Foreground remote compaction [records response completion](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/compact_remote_v2.rs#L429-L452), then [charges the rollout budget on installation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/compact_remote_v2_installation.rs#L185-L190) and [recomputes context usage](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/compact_remote_v2_installation.rs#L277-L279). It does not take the ordinary cumulative update path there.
4. **Optional rollout-budget fallback is not a cached-token cap.** [Without server-defined units, it counts weighted output plus uncached input](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/core/src/rollout_budget.rs#L48-L69). This module is byte-identical in the two inspected tags. No `codex_rollout_budget_units` values were present in the 8,003 ledger usage objects. This does not establish that a rollout budget was configured during the incident, nor identify a new regression.

## Reproducible accounting discrepancy

The response ledger totals **1,895,619,810** tokens; the positive legacy `token_count.info.total_token_usage` increments total **1,887,969,622** across 8,007 increments: a net difference of **7,650,188**.

Matching records by anonymous session and the complete six-field usage tuple gives:

- **15 unmatched ledger responses, all matching installed compaction response IDs: 8,166,478 tokens.**
- **19 unmatched legacy-counter increments: 516,290 tokens.** Their cause is not established here; they must not be silently discarded or described as additional billed responses.
- `8,166,478 - 516,290 = 7,650,188`, accounting for the entire difference.

For example, an installed compaction at **2026-10-18T08:41:48.322Z** in the measured parent turn records **535,305 input, 533,760 cached input, 6,915 output, 542,220 total**. No equal per-session legacy-counter increment exists in the dataset.

This is an observed reporting difference with a source-supported explanation for the compaction portion. Please confirm whether it is intentional and which user-facing totals use each representation. It does not prove duplicate billing or explain the main quota drain by itself.

## Offline reproduction and evidence checks

A sanitized evidence package has been prepared locally. It contains per-response records, positive legacy-counter increments, allowance snapshots, anonymous session/turn relationships, summary totals, the extractor, and a standard-library verifier. Maintainers can replay the accounting comparison without running a paid workload:

```text
python3 verify_evidence.py
PASS: 8,003 responses / 80 sessions / 1,895,619,810 ledger tokens
PASS: 15 compactions account for all 8,166,478 unmatched ledger tokens;
      19 unmatched counter increments total 516,290; net gap 7,650,188
PASS: October 18 turn and descendants: 538 responses / 131,435,002 tokens;
      same-reset weekly snapshots: 26% -> 67% used (account-level correlation)
```

A separate Rust probe compiles the **unmodified upstream `rollout_budget.rs`**, with supporting type stubs, and uses synthetic usage only:

```text
rustc --edition=2024 budget_probe.rs -o budget_probe
./budget_probe
fallback: 100,000,000 cached input + 100 output tokens exhaust a 100-unit budget on step 100
uncached control: same input with zero cache exhausts the budget on step 1
server-unit control: 10 supplied units per response exhaust the budget on step 10
```

This reproduces the optional client budget's fallback behavior, **not server billing or the original 10-point symptom**. It makes no network requests or model calls. The source file's SHA-256 is `d654675314ee5a7437164c657dc4850f91d5870cb5f446bf8a1f7d0df7f849b3`.

Extraction checks found **zero duplicate response IDs, zero ledger thread-attribution mismatches, zero counter decreases, zero malformed records, zero input-plus-output arithmetic mismatches, and zero files changed during extraction**. Selected metadata contains one creator account and one creator user; that does not identify an account for every resumed request.

The package excludes prompts, generated text, private code, tool arguments/results, original response/session/account IDs, project names, local paths, credentials, and credit balances. Exact event times, model/settings metadata and allowance percentages remain. The full ZIP is **not attached to this issue**; it is available through an agreed upload channel. The inline measurements above are provided now.

## Requested investigation and bounded reproduction

1. Reconcile server usage and allowance deductions for the October 18 interval above, including the parent, its three child sessions, cache weighting, model/reasoning settings, compactions and approval-review work. Original identifiers can be supplied privately if needed.
2. Check whether allocation or metering changed around October 16. Compare equivalent controlled workloads; the daily totals here cannot answer that question.
3. Clarify the compaction omission from the legacy cumulative counter and the 19 unmatched counter increments.
4. In an instrumented internal account, compare a fresh chat with a retained-history chat at fixed model/settings, using a deterministic, **capped** sequence of tool continuations. Record response IDs, per-response input/cache/output, compaction usage, and server allowance units. Run a separate bounded child-session variant. This is a proposed protocol, not a completed live reproduction.
5. Investigate whether per-turn work/usage visibility and enforceable spending limits can prevent hundreds of hidden continuations from exhausting allowance.

## Related reports

Original related report: #51088. The duplicate-detection bot suggested #54767, #54677 and #54868. #55168 independently documents repeated cached-context processing and related accounting questions; its totals are from a different user and are **not included in this dataset**. Please consolidate tracking if these share a root cause.

Evidence archive SHA-256: `bd09960f3d187d328de480967373485bd02f26d0c0d59b8686d14e233ecf263b`. Prepared size: 554953 bytes. The ZIP is not attached; the fingerprint identifies the local evidence package for a later agreed transfer.

items.body:
# Windows 桌面版：鼠标位于内嵌交互表格内时，滚轮无法带动聊天页面

## 环境

- Windows x64，Codex／ChatGPT 桌面应用。
- 观察到的 Windows 应用包版本：26.1013.4894.0。这是安装包版本，未把它当作“关于”窗口里的显示版本。
- 受影响的是聊天中的内嵌交互式 HTML 表格，使用底部按钮在原位置分页，每页显示 5 条。

## 问题

鼠标停留在表格区域内时，上下滚动鼠标滚轮，外层聊天页面不移动，容易给人应用卡住的感觉。用户在多次调整表格之后仍反复报告同样的问题。

## 建议复现步骤（请使用虚构占位数据）

1. 在 Windows 桌面应用的聊天里生成一个内嵌交互式 HTML 表格，只使用“示例 A”“示例 B”等虚构文本。
2. 设置为每页 5 条，底部按钮仅在当前表格中切换页面，不发送聊天消息。
3. 不设置表格内部的纵向滚动区域，让内容自然撑开。
4. 将鼠标停留在表格单元格上，向上、向下滚动滚轮；翻页后再重复。
5. 检查滚轮是否能继续带动外层聊天页面。

预期：表格没有自己的纵向滚动需求时，鼠标处于表格内也应能滚动整段聊天；原位置分页继续正常使用。

实际用户反馈：鼠标在表格内时，滚轮无法带动聊天页面。

## 已尝试与验证边界

- 移除了表内独立滚动容器及固定高度限制，并调整了文档溢出和表格宽度设置；用户反馈仍未解决。
- 普通浏览器中进行的本地预览测试可以滚动，但该测试不能证明桌面应用中的滚轮联动已正常。
- 本报告明确区分用户多次反馈与自动化独立复现：尚未在当前桌面聊天界面中用自动化独立核验，也未确认具体根因。
- 请排查内嵌交互窗口与外层聊天之间的滚轮传递。不要以更换为静态表格或用发送聊天消息代替原位置分页作为问题已修复的依据。

## 隐私范围

本报告只包含界面行为和应用包版本。不附任何实际表格内容、业务数据、商品名称、金额、截图、源文件、会话文本、会话链接或诊断日志。复现请使用虚构占位数据。

items.title: Blocking the initial UserPromptSubmit event causes an endless “Blocked by hook” loop

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

items.body:
## Description

When a `UserPromptSubmit` hook rejects the initial user prompt, Codex repeatedly displays “Blocked by hook” with the same rejection message instead of ending the submission and returning control to the user.

The rejection is intentional and persistent: the session or user is denied by policy, so the hook returns a blocking result for every event. **The first blocked event is `UserPromptSubmit`, before any model work or tool execution.**

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a `UserPromptSubmit` hook to always reject prompts with a blocking result and a reason.
2. Submit a prompt.
3. Keep the rejection condition unchanged.
4. Observe repeated “Blocked by hook” messages without submitting another prompt.

## Expected behavior

Codex should reject the prompt once, display the reason, and return control to the user. A persistent denial should not trigger automatic resubmission or an unbounded hook loop.

## Actual behavior

Codex repeatedly surfaces the same hook rejection and remains in a loop despite no new user input or change to the rejection condition.

## Related issues

These reports describe related loops, but **none covers this exact case: rejection of the initial prompt by `UserPromptSubmit`.**

- #37937 — Repeated blocking by a `Stop` hook causes an infinite loop.
- #34477 — `Stop` hook feedback injected as a prompt causes repeated model turns.
- #36503 — `PreToolUse` blocking causes repeated retries during goal execution.

## Environment

- Codex version: Not recorded
- Interface: Not recorded
- OS: Not recorded

items.title: Chrome side panel resets to GPT-6.1 Sol Light; web model preference persists but is not inherited

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### Affected surface

Official ChatGPT Chrome extension, browser side panel / Side Chat in Work mode. This is **not** the VS Code extension or a temporary side chat inside a desktop Codex task.

### Environment

- Observed on October 18, 2026
- Plan: ChatGPT Pro
- Browser/platform: Google Chrome on macOS
- Exact Chrome, extension, and desktop app versions: not collected

### Problem

Opening the Chrome extension for a new side-panel interaction repeatedly starts with **GPT-6.1 Sol / Light**. A different model or reasoning effort can be selected manually, but the reporter has not found a way to make that choice the starting default for later side-panel sessions.

Changing the model selection in ChatGPT Work on the web persists there, including after a reload and in a newly opened ChatGPT tab, but does not change the Chrome extension's starting selection.

### Observed workflow and reproduction

1. Open the official ChatGPT extension in Chrome.
2. Observe the starting model/effort: **GPT-6.1 Sol / Light**.
3. Manually choose a different model/effort in the side panel. A reporter-provided screenshot confirms the picker can display **GPT-6.1 Sol / High**.
4. Open the extension again for a fresh interaction; the reporter observes **Sol / Light** again.

Additional cross-surface test:

1. In the same Chrome browser, open `https://chatgpt.com/` in Work mode.
2. Explicitly select **GPT-6 Astra / Medium**.
3. Reload the web page: **Astra / Medium** remains selected.
4. Open ChatGPT in another tab: **Astra / Medium** remains selected there as well.
5. Ask the reporter to close and reopen the extension and check a new conversation.
6. The reporter confirms that the extension still shows **Sol / Light**.

### Evidence and scope

- Web persistence across reload and a new tab was directly checked through the visible UI.
- The extension's return to Sol / Light is the reporter's repeated observation; the side-panel UI itself was not accessible to the browser automation used for the web comparison.
- The provided side-panel screenshot shows a model submenu, effort slider, speed control, and reset icon. There is no save-default control visible in that first-level popover. The second-level menu has not been fully inspected.
- This report does **not** establish that the model of an existing saved conversation changes, that the backend runs a different model than displayed, or that all preferences should be shared across surfaces.
- No root cause has been identified. It is unclear whether this is a persistence bug or an intentional default with a missing configuration option.

### Expected behavior

Please provide a supported way to choose the starting model **and** reasoning effort for new Chrome side-panel conversations, such as:

- remembering the last explicit side-panel selection; or
- a persistent extension-specific default; or
- an explicit option to inherit the saved Work web preference.

A per-conversation override should remain possible. If resetting to Sol / Light is intentional, please document that behavior and expose how users can change the default.

### Impact

Users must manually reselect the model/effort whenever they start work through the extension. It is easy to submit a complex research or coding question at Light effort unintentionally.

### Related, but different scope

- #38442 requests separate defaults for temporary side chats inside the desktop app.
- #44678 requests Max effort availability in the Chrome side panel.

I searched the tracker for Chrome/side-panel model defaults, reset behavior, and model persistence and did not find a matching report for this specific cross-surface behavior. Please redirect this issue if the web-backed Chrome side panel is tracked elsewhere.

items.title: codex queue / hooks: wake an idle session with a non-user, attributed message

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI (codex-cli 0.164.0-alpha.3, Linux, interactive TUI)

### What feature would you like to see?

A supported way for a local script or another agent to send a message to a running, **idle** Codex session that:

1. starts a turn (wakes the session), and
2. is **not** presented as a user message, either in the TUI or to the model.

**Today**

- `codex queue --thread <id> --message <text>` wakes an idle session. But the item is user input. The TUI draws it exactly like an operator prompt (`› text` with the user-message background), and it reaches the model as `role: "user"`. `thread/queue/add` accepts only user input too.
- Hooks render distinctly and reach the model as developer context. `PostToolUse` shows `↳ Hook · <text>`, and `Stop` with `decision: "block"` shows `• Blocked by hook └ <text>`. But they only work during an active turn. A background hook that finishes while no turn is active waits for the next user turn and does not start one.

So when the recipient is idle, the only route is one that looks and acts like the human typed it. In a terminal with several agents messaging each other, the operator can no longer tell their own messages from agent traffic. The model also gets agent-written text at user authority.

**Request (any one would solve it)**

1. A non-user delivery kind for the queue, for example `codex queue --as developer --from "<label>"` (and the same field in `thread/queue/add`). The item starts a turn when the session is idle. It reaches the model as developer context, and the TUI draws it as an attributed notice (e.g. `↳ Message from <label> · <text>`), not as a user prompt.
2. Let a background command hook start a turn when the session is idle, for example on exit code 2 or a `wake: true` output field. Its `additionalContext` is delivered as developer context, and `systemMessage` is shown as a notice.

**Why it matters**

Local multi-agent setups need agent-to-agent messages that wake the recipient but keep provenance. That covers a worker reporting back to a coordinator, or a script relaying a result. Today the choice is between "wakes but impersonates the user" (`codex queue`) and "keeps provenance but cannot wake" (hooks).

### Additional information

Related, but not the same request:
- #45456: agent-authored queued content becomes `role: "user"` (provenance loss, from the subagent side).
- #38221: allow an async `Stop` hook to start a same-session continuation.
- #48928: steer mode for `codex queue`.

items.title: Archiving a thread does not shut down its title-generation thread and prediction fork; each keeps a full stdio MCP set for ~30 min

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

26.1013.40934 (build 20770), bundled `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 arm (macOS 26.2 25C56, MacBook Air M4, 16 GB)

### What issue are you seeing?

Every new thread in Codex Desktop starts **three** threads, and each one starts a full set of stdio MCP servers:

| Thread | When it appears | Stopped by archiving the parent? | When its MCP set goes away |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The thread itself | `thread/start` | Yes, immediately | On archive |
| Title-generation thread (ephemeral, `gpt-6-luna`, effort `low`) | ~1 s after `thread/start` | **No** | ~30 min later (idle unload) |
| Composer prediction fork (`thread/fork`, `experimentalPredictionMode`) | After the first turn | **No** | ~30 min later (idle unload) |

Archiving a thread only shuts down that thread. Its title-generation thread and prediction fork keep running with their full MCP sets for another ~30 minutes, even though they only exist to serve the archived thread and never call a tool.

Two examples from `~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite`, times relative to `thread/start` of the user thread:

| Event | Example A | Example B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User thread `thread/start` | T+0 s | T+0 s |
| Ephemeral title thread created, MCP set spawned | T+1 s | T+1 s |
| Title thread outputs its message / parent thread renamed | T+5 s / T+5 s | T+5 s / T+6 s |
| Prediction fork created, MCP set spawned | T+6 s | T+7 s |
| `thread/archive` then `op.dispatch.shutdown` (user thread's own MCP set is terminated) | T+225 s | T+9 s |
| Title thread `op.dispatch.shutdown`, its MCP set exits | **T+1805 s** | **T+1805 s** |
| Prediction fork `op.dispatch.shutdown`, its MCP set exits | **T+1812 s** | **T+1815 s** |

Impact on this machine: with ~21 configured stdio servers (mostly `npx -y <pkg>`), one set is about 29 processes and 1.2 GB `phys_footprint`, about half of it in `npm exec` wrapper processes. I created 10 threads (one "hi" each) and archived all of them within ~4.5 minutes. The summed `phys_footprint` of the app-server's MCP descendants peaked at **22.5 GB** on this 16 GB machine. After archiving it stayed between **15 and 18 GB** for ~26 minutes, until the helper threads unloaded around T+30 min, and then fell to 3.6 GB. That 3.6 GB baseline is three older idle threads that existed before the test. Codex was visibly sluggish during the bursts.

I matched each MCP set to its thread by spawn time (one `chrome-devtools-mcp` process per set) against `thread/start`, `thread/fork`, and the first log line of each ephemeral thread ID (UUIDv7 creation time). The title thread has no `thread/start` log line and no `thread-writer-locks` file, so it is easy to miss.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure several stdio MCP servers (for example 5–10 `npx -y …` servers).
2. In Codex Desktop, create a new thread and send `hi`. Wait for the reply and for the title to appear.
3. Archive the thread immediately.
4. Watch the app-server's direct children, for example `ps -o pid,lstart,args -p $(pgrep -P <app-server pid>)`.
5. One MCP set exits at archive time. Two more sets, spawned ~1 s and ~6 s after the thread was created, stay alive for ~30 minutes.

### What is the expected behavior?

1. Archiving or deleting a thread should also shut down the ephemeral helper threads created for it (title generation, prediction forks), or at least drop their subscription so they unload right away.
2. Better, helper threads that never call tools should not start stdio MCP servers at all. A title or prediction only needs the cached tool catalog, not live processes.

### Additional information

Code pointers (`rust-v0.163.0`, commit `8308618`):

- Archive shuts down only the thread and its spawn subtree: [`thread_processor.rs` L1722–L1788](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L1722-L1788) (`state_db_spawn_subtree_thread_ids` → `prepare_thread_for_removal`). The title thread and prediction forks are not in that subtree.
- Every non-subagent thread starts MCP eagerly: [`mcp_runtime.rs` L380–L384](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/session/mcp_runtime.rs#L380-L384).
- In the desktop bundle, the metadata-generation helper (title, description, summary, commit/PR message) starts an ephemeral read-only thread with `ephemeralGenerationModel` and a config override that disables only `mcp_servers.codex_app`. All user-configured MCP servers stay enabled in that thread.

Related: #30408 (canonical MCP accumulation), #54700 (prediction forks start MCP), #39783 (ephemeral summary threads keep full MCP stacks), and the draft tool-free thread mode in #31922, which would cover the title thread.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Windows running binary ProductVersion/FileVersion: `155.0.8059.80`. This was read from the executable's version metadata; the About dialog was not opened, so its displayed version is unverified.

Installed Computer Use skill bundle: `computer-use/26.1013.40934`, using `@oai/sky` through `node_repl`. Separately installed CLI reports `codex-cli 0.156.0`; this is not asserted to be the desktop's bundled backend version.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report. The user describes themselves as a heavy user.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, x64, version `10.0.26200`, build `26200`. The target Electron renderer reported device scale factor `1.5`. Captured window origins included negative desktop X coordinates. Their relevance to the failure is unconfirmed.

### What issue are you seeing?

**Primary user complaint:** “几乎全是失败操作，而且失败了，也不释放窗口” — “Almost all the operations fail, and after they fail, the windows are not released.” The user reports an extremely poor Windows Computer Use experience and says this is becoming intolerable even for a heavy user. Please treat the combination of low task success and failure to promptly release the user's desktop/resources as the central issue.

Windows Computer Use could open and capture an application's native folder selector but could not reliably target its controls or enter the folder path. A simple folder-selection task turned into a prolonged sequence of snapshots, focus attempts and failed actions, while the application, native dialog and test services occupied the user's machine.

This report covers both a concrete tool inconsistency and poor agent recovery behavior. It does not assert that every failed action was a Computer Use implementation defect.

Observed tool behavior:

- An Electron board window owned a project-settings window, which in turn opened a native Windows folder-selection dialog. `sky.list_windows()` exposed the board as the Electron target, but did not expose the settings window or the native selector as separately selectable windows.
- `sky.get_window_state()` for the returned board nevertheless showed screenshots and accessibility entries for the owned settings window and folder dialog, including an editable Folder control.
- Attempting `sky.set_value()` on the Folder control's index from that observation failed with: `element 464 is not available in cached app state for electron.exe`.
- Screenshot-based clicks intended for the folder field, and attempts to navigate the address field, did not yield reliable focus. The reported focused element remained a SearchEditBox; captures showed the owner active while the native modal appeared inactive. This is observed behavior, not a confirmed root cause.
- One screenshot-based native Cancel action succeeded and the test database remained unchanged. Reopening the selector still did not produce reliable folder entry/selection.
- A later call returned: `Computer Use was stopped by the user with the physical Escape key. Stop your work, do not call further Computer Use tools in this turn, and send a final message noting that the user stopped Computer Use.` No further Computer Use calls were made after that result.

Agent failure and user impact:

- Repeated recovery attempts consumed substantial attention and left windows open without completing a basic selection/input operation. The agent should have stopped these attempts much earlier.
- Resource occupancy mattered: the user did not consent to their desktop and background resources being consumed indefinitely simply because testing had previously been authorized.
- Automatic Goal continuation generated further turns after desktop interaction had been stopped. Those turns did not resume Computer Use, but the continuation mechanism still required additional coordination to avoid repeated no-progress wakeups. A stopped desktop dependency should be surfaced as a durable blocked condition.

The user explicitly asked that OpenAI's developers hear this severity, not just receive an apology:

> 你这个 computer use 在 Windows 上使用的效果是非常非常差的，这一点你要让 OpenAI 的开发者知道，再这样下去，连我这边的重度用户都受不了了。

Translation: “The experience of using Computer Use on Windows is extremely, extremely poor. OpenAI's developers need to know this. If this continues, even a heavy user like me cannot put up with it.”

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is an observed failure sequence, not a claim of a newly rerun minimal reproduction. Desktop interaction has been stopped at the user's instruction.

1. On Windows, attach Computer Use to an Electron application's board window using the actual returned Window object.
2. Open an owned settings window and invoke an owned native directory selector from it.
3. Compare `sky.list_windows()` with `sky.get_window_state({ window: board, include_screenshot: true, include_text: true })`. In this session, the modal was visible in state but not independently returned as a window.
4. Use the Folder edit element index from the fresh state with `sky.set_value`. The observed result was the cached-app-state error above.
5. Try a screenshot-grounded click on the folder field and re-observe focus. In this session, reliable folder-field focus/path input was not achieved.

Exact app source, user directories, private project data, raw screenshots and the complete session transcript are intentionally omitted. No additional reproduction run was started to prepare this report.

### What is the expected behavior?

1. Every owned modal visible in a snapshot should either be targetable through a returned window/control identity, or be explicitly marked non-actionable with a precise reason. Actionable accessibility indexes should agree with the action cache.
2. Target activation must preserve the intended owned modal and provide trustworthy focus verification for typing, including multi-window/negative-coordinate/DPI cases.
3. Recovery should be bounded. After repeated failure without new evidence, the agent should stop interaction and release its own idle resources rather than repeatedly capturing and clicking.
4. Physical Esc and subsequent user instructions must remain effective across automatic Goal continuations; the same blocked UI dependency should not repeatedly wake the agent.
5. A basic folder-selection task should complete promptly, or fail clearly and promptly, without monopolizing the user's computer.

### Additional information

Observed on 2026-10-18, UTC+08:00. The application under test used isolated QA data. Independent readback before resource cleanup showed revision `1`, no workspace binding and no directory-binding write. The verified QA application and its child processes were terminated only for resource cleanup; the two test services shut down through their stop markers. Subsequent readback confirmed those PIDs absent and their connection descriptors removed. This cleanup is not claimed as normal application-close acceptance.

No credentials, private repository URLs, LAN addresses, account identifiers, raw logs or full conversation content are attached. Please triage both the Windows owned-dialog/control targeting failure and the agent's no-progress/resource-management behavior.
